title: iOS: Boot splash is drawn at 1× scale and upscaled, so it looks blurry on Retina screens
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable (official export templates, Mobile renderer, Metal). - The code involved is unchanged on `master`. ### System information iPhone 13 mini (iPhone14,4), iOS 27.0.1, screen scale 3. Exported from macOS 15.6.1 with Xcode 26.3. ### Issue description On iOS, the boot splash is drawn into a swap chain sized in points instead of pixels (812×375 instead of 2436×1125 on this device). Core Animation then upscales it 3× to fill the screen, so the splash image looks blurry. Every frame after the splash is sharp. To make this measurable, I used a 2436×1125 splash image made of 1-pixel black and white stripes with a thin red border, with `stretch_mode` set to Disabled so it should map 1:1 to screen pixels. I took an on-device screenshot (side button + volume up) while the boot splash was showing, then a second one while a normal frame drew the same image 1:1 with a `TextureRect`, marked with a thick green border. The results below come from the attached MRP. - Normal frame: a row reads `0, 255, 0, 255, 0, 255, …`, which is a 1:1 mapping. - Boot splash: the same row reads `0, 84, 170, 255, 170, 84, 0, …`. That is a period-6 triangle wave: every third stripe sampled, then magnified 3× with linear filtering. The vertical direction shows the same pattern. The red 3 px border around the image is fully visible, so the image is not cropped, only drawn at a third of the resolution. | Boot splash (crop, 8× nearest) | Normal frame (crop, 8× nearest) | | --- | --- | | | | **Probable cause** In the `DisplayServerAppleEmbedded` constructor, the rendering context's window size is set from the layer bounds times the screen scale ([`display_server_apple_embedded.mm`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/drivers/apple_embedded/display_server_apple_embedded.mm#L140)): ```cpp Size2i size = Size2i(layer.bounds.size.width, layer.bounds.size.height) * screen_get_max_scale(); rendering_context->window_set_size(DisplayServerEnums::MAIN_WINDOW_ID, size.width, size.height); ``` `screen_get_max_scale()` calls the virtual `screen_get_scale()`, which `DisplayServerIOS` overrides to return `[UIScreen mainScreen].scale`. Because the call happens in the base class constructor, it dispatches to `DisplayServer::screen_get_scale()`, which returns 1.0. The swap chain is therefore created in points. `Main::setup2()` then draws the boot splash into this surface (`RendererCompositorRD::set_boot_image_with_stretch()`). Only later does `layoutRenderingLayer` call `resize_window()`, which now runs after construction, gets the correct scale, and resizes the swap chain. That is why everything after the splash is sharp. A possible fix is to compute the scale in the constructor without virtual dispatch, for example by reading `[UIScreen mainScreen].scale` (or the view's `contentScaleFactor`) directly. Another option is to resize the window once construction is complete, before the boot splash is drawn. Related, but different: #81389 is about whether the boot splash shows on iOS at all, depending on the renderer. #82730 was about the screen size being detected wrongly for the whole game. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the attached MRP and export it for iOS. The Mobile renderer and the default landscape orientation are already set. Its splash is a 2436×1125 stripe pattern (iPhone 13 mini resolution in landscape), with `boot_splash/stretch_mode` set to Disabled. 2. Run it on an iPhone with a 3× screen. The main scene pauses the render loop for 10 seconds, so the boot splash stays on screen. 3. Take an on-device screenshot while the pattern has a thin red border: that is the boot splash. The stripes are blurred into grey bands. 4. After 10 seconds, the same pattern is drawn 1:1 by a normal frame, with a thick green border. Take a second screenshot: the stripes are sharp. On a device with another resolution, the stripes still show the problem, but the pattern is not 1:1, so the comparison between the two screenshots is the meaningful part. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [ios-splash-scale-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33600557/ios-splash-scale-mrp.zip)
